# Shared fixed R Git integration

28 October 2026, Europe/Berlin. SPEC/TEST ONLY. Runtime remains held.

The selected operation is `_original_r_git_checks(account, timer, *, api=None, tool=None)`. Exactly one mode, api or tool, is supplied per invocation. Both internal call sites remain. Preparation uses api; `_verify_original_r_live(account, prepared, tool, timer)` uses tool. No command callable, arbitrary path, environment, cap or fault interface escapes. Reuse W3's nested Git lifecycle, parsers, inventories and stable readers together. Keep W2's actual row owners, W4's proof/account/finalizer, the 23 unamended original owners byte-exact, and W4's three accepted original amendments.

Preparation creates/registers its four roots, acquires API metadata, initializes, fetches and checks out under its existing Timer360. Live does none of these effects and uses retained authenticated metadata. Live uses the supplied original Timer1200, its unchanged end, pending/expired state and account deadline. It cannot reuse preparation.deadline_ns, reset any allowance, enter another Timer, or erase preparation.complete after a later failure. Each Git child retains the existing 15-second cleanup reserve and all original resource/ownership/pipe/reap rules.

The preparation environment has exactly SEVEN keys. HOME, TMPDIR, PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, LANG=C.UTF-8, LC_ALL=C.UTF-8, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1. Live uses exactly the OTHER seven keys from all four authoritative W2 vectors. HOME, TMPDIR, PATH=tool.uv.parent:/usr/bin:/bin, LC_ALL=C.UTF-8, VIRTUAL_ENV, SPECFACT_MODULES_REPO and SPECFACT_MODULES_ROOTS. No extra NOSYSTEM, LANG or host environment is allowed. Effective config under the live environment must have exactly W3's four local core values with exact scope/origin framing and no duplicates. NOSYSTEM suppresses system configuration only; it does not suppress HOME/.gitconfig.

Both live boundaries enforce W3's owned-root identities, detached fixed R HEAD, fixed C shallow boundary, absent refs, strict fsck, actual R bytes and signature/payload relation, R/C trees and ancestry, exact governed diff and rename rules, stage-zero index/tree equality, H flags, clean tracked diff, ten pinned source blobs/stable files, and forbidden Git metadata. They execute before rows and after binder inside the existing original materializer. Preserve command96 and metadata64000 cumulatively. Count the finite preparation plus two-live sequence before code acceptance. Current W3 has 35 invocations. A direct live reuse with one config check and one refs check, skipping init/fetch/checkout and retaining status, has 28. Thus 35 + 28 + 28 = 91 fits command96 statically. This is a proposed finite sequence, not actual code or workload fit. The minimum cache reconciliation below requires independent review before CODE.

Keep the initial `caches()` capture and attachment before the first live verifier. Move the existing final `caches()` capture and attachment immediately BEFORE the second live verifier, after the existing safe point, under the same original Timer1200, account, category admission and cumulative debits. This is an ordering dependency, not an additional inventory, helper, launcher or cap. Retained current cache facts use the existing encoded `(label, relativepath, bytecount, sha)` records in the C/M/R namespace. The trusted sequential owner captures current facts immediately before verification; this is not atomic filesystem containment and does not claim to detect hostile same-UID or concurrent mutation inside an already matched collapsed directory.

Before API metadata setattr, captured chunk append, receipt assignment, or final binary/inventory tuple append, require preparation.metadata_bytes + account.metadata_bytes + actual_new_bytes <= 8388608 - 65536 bytes. Keep both subtotals cumulative and debit actual copies. Pipe capture separately reserves 65536 bytes for the pending receipt, so its capacity is at most 8388608 - 65536 footer - 65536 receipt - both subtotals. A refusal permanently stops the account without attaching refused bytes. Finalizer serialization retains its already accepted separate copy debits.
